discover_titles: Trump's Russia Move: Why He Waived Oil Tariffs
U.S. Policy Shift: Trump Halts Sanctions on Russian Oil Buyers
Zelenskyy Slams Trump's Decision to Ease Russian Energy Pressure
spot: President Trump has waived new sanctions on Russia and significant tariffs on the world's largest buyers of Russian oil and natural gas, reversing a bipartisan law aimed at pressuring Moscow. The decision, made late Friday, seeks to ease energy prices but drew criticism from Ukraine.
content_html:
Key Developments

President Trump late Friday prevented new sanctions on Russia and substantial tariffs on large-scale buyers of Russian oil and natural gas from taking effect. This action involved waiving portions of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act, a bipartisan law Mr. Trump signed last month, which was designed to exert pressure on the Russian government.

Under the Graham Act, 100% tariffs on the world's five largest importers of Russian crude oil and natural gas were scheduled to begin on Sunday. Additionally, the law included 500% tariffs on Russian goods and other sanctions. However, the legislation grants the president authority to waive these provisions if he certifies to Congress that halting the sanctions is "in the national interests of the United States," a clause Mr. Trump invoked via an executive order Friday. He confirmed sending a notification to Congress regarding this decision.

The waivers are set to remain in place until administration officials deem further action necessary, with directives for monitoring countries importing Russian energy or evading sanctions. Kirill Dmitriev, an envoy to Russian President Vladimir Putin, lauded the decision on Saturday, calling it an "important and truly historic moment." In contrast, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the move as "unfortunate," stating the Graham Act "could have helped enormously" and that a "U.S. sanctions blackout, easing pressure on the aggressor, financial rewards for Putin - all of this only encourages him to keep attacking."

The Graham Act primarily targeted major buyers of Russian oil and gas, including China, India, and Turkey. While the European Union historically purchased significant quantities, it has reduced imports in recent years. These waivers follow Mr. Trump's earlier action one week prior, when he eased sanctions on Russian diesel and announced a deal with President Putin to import diesel into the U.S. market.

Key Takeaways

  • President Trump invoked national interest to waive new sanctions and 100% tariffs on the largest global buyers of Russian oil and natural gas.
  • The waivers also halted 500% tariffs on Russian goods and other sanctions, reversing a bipartisan law aimed at pressuring Russia.
  • The decision was praised by a Russian envoy but strongly condemned by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who warned it would encourage further aggression.

Why It Matters

President Trump's decision marks a significant about-face in United States policy towards Russia, shifting from a stance of tight restrictions and pressure to one of easing sanctions and tariffs. This move, justified by the administration as a means to ease energy prices, could have profound implications for global energy markets and geopolitical dynamics. By reducing financial pressure on Russia and its major energy clients, the waivers risk undermining international efforts to hold Moscow accountable for its actions, particularly in Ukraine.

The reversal also highlights a divergence from the original intent of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act, which sought to use economic leverage against the Russian government. The reactions from both Russian and Ukrainian officials underscore the contentious nature of the decision, with Moscow viewing it as a diplomatic victory and Kyiv seeing it as a detrimental step that could embolden further aggression.
